land.text: Macedon and the Thracian lands round Lysimachia, where Seleucus crossed the Hellespont in September 281 and was murdered by Keraunos

predecessors.note: kingdom-of-lysimachus names the heir 'Ptolemy Keraunos (Macedon and Thrace, 281-279)' as its European counterpart; Cliopatria's Lysimachus row ends 282.

land.text: Macedon, taken by Antigonus Gonatas after Lysimachia (277 BC) and, on antigonid-dynasty's reading of the Gonatas page, 'most of' it by the end of 276

successors.note: Cliopatria's Antigonid Macedonia row starts in 277.

capitals.name: Pella
capitals.note: No page opened names a capital for 281-277 (the Keraunos page names none; Keraunos was acclaimed at Lysimachia). Pella is Macedon's traditional seat and the antigonid-dynasty dossier's capital from 277/276; the coordinates are Pella's.

rulers.name: Ptolemy Keraunos
rulers.note: Murdered Seleucus in September 281, acclaimed king by the troops at Lysimachia; killed in early 279 after seventeen months.

rulers.name: Meleager
rulers.note: Succeeded his brother immediately but was deposed by his troops within months (Keraunos page, paraphrased).

rulers.name: Sosthenes
rulers.note: Infobox 'Reign: 279-277 BC'; 'Died: 277 BC'; 'may have declined the title of king'.
rulers.title: strategos or king (disputed)

correction.text: Macedon and the Thracian lands of Lysimachus's European half, held by Ptolemy Keraunos after the murder of Seleucus

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row for Macedon in 281-278 (Lysimachus ends 282, 'Antigonid Dynasty' draws only Antigonus Gonatas's Greek garrisons 284-278, 'Antigonid Macedonia' starts 277). The Keraunos page defines no territory: 'briefly king of Macedon', troops at Lysimachia proclaimed him king, and he sought control of Lysimachus's former lands; the shape is Ancient Macedon, Greek East Macedonia and Thrace and the Lysimachia peninsula (41,500 km2), the same lands as kingdom-of-lysimachus's 281 loss less Thessaly, which the Keraunos page does not give him (Gonatas was confined to Demetrias, in Thessaly).

correction.text: Macedon alone, under Meleager, Antipater Etesias and Sosthenes, who beat Bolgius and faced Brennus 'in the summer of 279 BC'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Thracian part is dropped from 279 as a bridge (confidence 1): the Gauls under Bolgius invaded in January or February 279 BC (Keraunos page, paraphrased) and their survivors settled in Thrace (Tylis, 278). No page opened says who held Lysimachia after 279. Ancient Macedon is 25,500 km2 by the gazetteer; the pages give no area.

region.text: Macedon and the Thracian lands round Lysimachia

ledger.note: 281: Ptolemy Keraunos becomes king of Macedon and Thrace. Seleucus crossed the Hellespont in 'September 281 BC' and Keraunos murdered him at Argos; troops at Lysimachia proclaimed him king (paraphrased). The Keraunos page does not date the acclamation and gives no territory; the land is the researcher's reading of Lysimachus's European half.

279: the Gauls invade Macedon. The Gauls under Bolgius invaded in January or February 279 BC (Keraunos page, paraphrased); Keraunos died in battle against them in early 279 BC after a reign of seventeen months; Brennus's host followed 'in the summer of 279 BC' (Sosthenes page).

279: Meleager succeeds his brother. Meleager succeeded his brother immediately but was deposed by his troops within months (Keraunos page, paraphrased), a ruler change in the same state (the months are not given).
279: Antipater Etesias is king for 45 days. Infobox 'Reign: 279 BC (45 days)'; he was 'deposed by Sosthenes'.
279: Sosthenes takes command. Infobox 'Reign: 279-277 BC'; he 'may have declined the title of king'; he beat Bolgius, then 'was soon faced with the invasion of Brennus in the summer of 279 BC'.

region.text: Thrace and the Lysimachia peninsula, overrun by the Gauls

ledger.note: 279 (bridge): Thrace passes out of the state. The Gallic invasion page has the survivors of the host settle in Thrace and found 'a short-lived city-state named Tyle' (Tylis, 278 on the Comontorius page); no page opened says who held Lysimachia or the Thracian coast after Keraunos's death.
277: the Gallic wave ends. 'In 277 BC, Antigonus II Gonatas defeated the Gauls at the Battle of Lysimachia and the survivors retreated' (Gallic invasion page); Sosthenes 'Died: 277 BC'.

277: Sosthenes dies and Antigonus Gonatas takes Macedon. The Sosthenes page names Antigonus II Gonatas as successor without a date; Gonatas 'defeated the Gauls in a battle near Lysimachia, Thrace, in 277 BC' (Keraunos page).

wars.name: Gallic invasion of the Balkans

zones.text: Macedon, invaded in 279 and cleared by 277

wars.outcome: Bolgius's Gauls killed Keraunos in early 279; Sosthenes beat Bolgius and faced Brennus's invasion in summer 279; Antigonus Gonatas beat the Gauls at Lysimachia in 277.
wars.note: The Gallic invasion page: 'Bolgios inflicted heavy losses on the Macedonians, whose young king, Ptolemy Keraunos, was captured and decapitated'; the Keraunos page has him die in battle (paraphrased).

wars.name: Antigonus Gonatas's invasion of Macedonia
wars.outcome: 'Antigonus II Gonatas tried to invade Macedonia from Asia in 278 but was beaten by Sosthenes' (Sosthenes page); no ground changed hands.
wars.note: No Wikipedia article for the episode; the antigonid-dynasty dossier's 277 gain follows it.

wars.name: War of Ptolemy Keraunos against Epigonos and Monunius
wars.outcome: The page says only that this war 'seems to have occupied Ptolemy Ceraunus for most of 280 BC'; neither the land nor the result is on the page.
wars.note: Recorded so the 280 campaign is not silent; Keraunos also beat Antigonus Gonatas at sea and confined him to Demetrias (undated).

certainty.note: No page gives any frontier of Macedon in these years; the shapes are regions and the Thracian part is a bridge.

notes: Four pages. A state Cliopatria lacks and the eu-02-a notes call out: nobody owned Macedon between the end of Lysimachus (281) and Antigonid Macedonia (277). It has no Wikipedia article of its own; the identity's title is the kingdom's. The four rulers (Keraunos, Meleager, Antipater Etesias, Sosthenes) are one state by rule 2, entered as rename events with no months (no months are recorded; the order is Meleager, Antipater Etesias, Sosthenes). Pages differ on Antipater (the Keraunos page does not mention him; the Antipater page says Meleager was ousted before him) and on Sosthenes's title (strategos or king). Territory is the weak point: no page opened gives one, so the first shape follows kingdom-of-lysimachus's loss of Macedon and Thrace minus Thessaly and the second keeps Macedon alone. kingdom-of-lysimachus's 281 loss names the counterpart 'Ptolemy Keraunos (Macedon and Thrace, 281-279)' and antigonid-dynasty's 277 gain names 'Sosthenes (Macedon, 279-277)'; both now correspond to this slug. Pyrrhus's share of western Macedon (to 284) and Epirus's 274 conquest are on other dossiers. Not on any page opened: the capital, the detail of Keraunos's war of 280, the fate of Lysimachia after 279. The 280 war is only a war entry (no zone), because the page names neither land nor result.
